arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: the side that brought the case's advocate stated the stop-time rule specifies exactly what the government must do.
The government's advocate stated the stop-time rule may be triggered by a notice lacking a hearing date.
Justice Kagan questioned why ten requirements define a notice to appear if one is missing.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the legal definition of a valid notice to appear. The core issue is whether the absence of a hearing date invalidates the document for stop-time rule purposes.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: the side that brought the case wants the Court to hold that a notice without a hearing date does not trigger the stop-time rule.
The government wants the Court to hold that a notice without a hearing date still triggers the stop-time rule.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: the side that brought the case argues the stop-time rule requires a specific hearing date to end continuous presence.
The government argues the stop-time rule triggers upon service of a notice, regardless of a missing hearing date.
